review_scope: Independent AI-assisted English passage review of every proposed source/target pair against the exact cached Saints verse records. Snapshot byte verification belongs to the root review.
checks: Read all 59 source passages, target passages, and rationales. Every source and target ID resolves in cache-exact records; source coverage is exact and pair keys are unique.

Genealogy comparisons retain Asa/Asaph, Amon/Amos, Arran/Ram, Salman/Salmon, Azariah/Uzziah, and Joathan/Jotham wording differences. Compressed royal generations and Luke ancestry differences are explicitly acknowledged.
The Rahab maternity statement is not attributed to Ruth; no shared-name identity is manufactured for Matthew 1:14-15, which remain deferred.

Quoted prophecy references use the supplied Greek-based inventory: Micah 5:1; Jeremiah 38:15; royal Psalm 71:10-11. Isaiah 7:14 wording and Hosea 11:1 children-versus-Son wording differences are accurately disclosed.

Internal Matthew narrative links are labelled as same-chapter or same-book developments rather than independent corroboration. Luke infancy links explicitly preserve chronology and detail differences.
Exodus 4:19-20 and Genesis 46:2-4 comparison rationales accurately distinguish persons and travel destinations. The royal-threat comparison to Exodus 1 is limited to violence against male children.
Matthew 2:23 links establish Nazareth identification without inventing a direct Old Testament source for He will be called a Nazarene.

optional_wording_suggestions.suggestion: For maximal grammatical clarity, phrase the Matthew qualification as Joseph is Mary's husband, and Jesus was born of Mary. The current of whom formulation reproduces the verse but can sound ambiguous after husband. This is a wording clarification, not an evidence failure.
optional_wording_suggestions.resolution: Applied in the final proposal and retained pair.

limitations: This is peer AI-assisted English passage review, not independent human specialist, critical-text, historical, or live destination-anchor review.
